ideas.title: One cell in a clam shell, and my beak shakes the bubbles off
ideas.goal: The player builds ONE cell (two plates of their choice in a clam shell of sea water, plate size and gap set by where they put them), wires a thin wire across it and watches it work and tire: the wire glows, hydrogen bubbles crowd the copper, the glow sinks; a shake of the shell knocks the bubbles off and the glow comes back. Fun because the cell is alive in your hands and you learn to keep it going.
ideas.toward: Road step 2 itself (the cell): EMF from the two metals' electrode potentials in sea water, internal resistance from plate area, gap and sea water's conductivity (~5 S/m), polarisation from the bubbles' cover of the cathode; it plugs into circuit.jl as its Cell, so every later step runs on it.
ideas.idea: Bubbles nucleate on the copper at the rate the current makes hydrogen (Faraday's law), grow and stick until buoyancy or a shake frees them; the covered area raises the resistance. One continuous close shot, no variants side by side: Lumi's beak sets the plates in, touches the wire on, it glows, dims under the bubbles, Lumi grabs the shell and shakes, it flares again.
ideas.form: physics/cell.jl + the cell on the motor bench in Jump in; a path traced close film where Lumi's beak does every step.

ideas.title: The wire I drew burns out where I rushed it
ideas.goal: The player pulls a copper rod through smaller and smaller holes in a stone plate with Lumi's beak; each pass the wire gets longer and thinner; rush a pass (too big a step) and it necks or snaps, a worn hole leaves a thin stretch. That wire is then the wire of every circuit they build, and the thin stretch they rushed is where it glows first and parts. Fun because a craft you get good at pays off, or bites you, later.
ideas.toward: Road step 9 (every part made on the island) and step 1's circuit.jl: per-segment wire radius from the drawing, so the drawn wire's flaws decide where a coil overheats and where a filament parts.
ideas.idea: Drawing stress by Sachs' formula from the area reduction, die angle and friction, against copper's work-hardened flow stress (wire.jl's Hollomon law): over the limit it necks and snaps; the hole wears by drawn length so later wire comes out fatter or uneven; each segment keeps its radius. Seen: Lumi braced against a stone, hauling a gleaming wire out of a hole, the wire lengthening; later the same wire across the cells glowing at one bright spot.
ideas.form: physics/draw.jl + per-segment radius in circuit.jl + a workbench plugin; film of the hauling and of the bright spot.

ideas.title: I crank, and the light pushes back
ideas.goal: The player cranks the potter's wheel with the motor on it, by Lumi's legs or the keys: slow, nothing; faster, the wire on its leads goes red, and the crank gets heavy just as it glows; ease off and it darkens. Fun because you feel the light in your own effort and learn how hard light is to make.
ideas.toward: Road step 5 (the motor on the wheel as a generator) in one loop of motor.jl (motional EMF, back torque, energy holds) and circuit.jl (heat, glow).
ideas.idea: The crank is driven by Lumi's body: a muscle with Hill's force-velocity curve, so the faster it turns the less torque Lumi has, and the generator's back torque (from the current the glowing wire draws) is what slows it; Lumi's pose strains with the real load. Seen: a bird pedalling harder and harder as a wire goes cherry red, then puffing out of breath and the glow dying.
ideas.form: Plugin on the potter's wheel with Lumi's crank pose driven by the load + a path traced dusk film.

ideas.title: Copper grows on a nail
ideas.goal: The player crushes green rock, soaks it in the island's vinegar (fermented fruit) and drops an iron nail in: a skin of copper grows on it, real copper they can scrape off and melt into a rod. The more rock and the longer it soaks, the more copper. Fun as alchemy that works.
ideas.toward: Road step 9 (copper from green rock): malachite dissolves in acetic acid as copper acetate; iron displaces copper from solution (cementation), the first copper on the island made, not found.
ideas.idea: Dissolution rate from grain size and acid strength, the solution's blue-green from its copper concentration, cementation rate on the iron's area; the nail turns pink-copper and the liquid fades from blue-green to pale. Seen: a blue-green bowl, a grey nail going copper over a time-lapse in Lumi's beak.
ideas.form: physics/leach.jl + a bowl at the kiln + a path traced time-lapse film.

ideas.title: My first light, carried through the dark
ideas.goal: The player puts a filament of their own wire into a glass bulb they blew, connects it to their cells and carries the lit bulb through the night to the friends; air in the bulb eats the filament and it fails at its thinnest spot, mid-walk, unless they sealed it. Fun because it is your own light, and you have to get it there.
ideas.toward: Circuit.jl's heat and fusing at the thinnest spot, the cells' plate size deciding the brightness; a lamp for the cart later.
ideas.idea: Filament temperature from circuit.jl; its colour and power from Planck's law into a Hikari light inside real glass; copper oxidises at that temperature (parabolic oxide growth) thinning the wire until it parts. Seen: Lumi walking a glowing bulb through the dark, faces of the friends lighting up as it passes, then a flash and black.
ideas.form: Plugin + a night tracking film following Lumi (moving light, never a fixed camera on an object alone).

ideas.title: The wire's song
ideas.goal: A thin wire stretched over the motor's stones hums when AC from the cranked generator runs through it: tighten it and the note rises, at the right tension it sings loud because it resonates with the current. The player tunes it like a string. Fun as an instrument made from the cart's parts.
ideas.toward: Fields push any conductor (em.jl I dl x B on a string), the generator's AC frequency from the crank speed, a check of the solver's forces by ear.
ideas.idea: The wire as a tensioned string (wave equation, its modes from tension and mass per length), driven by I x B at the current's frequency; resonance when the crank's frequency matches a mode; the sound synthesised from the string's motion. Seen and heard: a wire blurring into a standing wave and humming.
ideas.form: physics/string.jl + sound + a film with sound.
